question: What methods and empirical phenomena define developmental interpretability of language models, and how might following representations and circuits through training support earlier safety intervention?

key_findings.claim: The review defines developmental interpretability by its longitudinal object of study rather than by a new analysis method.
key_findings.evidence: Its taxonomy contrasts behavior analysis, post-hoc mechanistic analysis of final weights, and repeated probing, patching, or circuit analysis across training checkpoints to ask how mechanisms form and change.

key_findings.claim: The central synthesis organizes training dynamics around circuit composition, biphasic knowledge-circuit formation, capability phase transitions, and competition between in-context and in-weights strategies.
key_findings.evidence: Sections 3.1–3.5 connect induction-head composition, a formation-to-optimization shift in continual pretraining, loss-threshold accounts of emergence, transient ICL, and grokking as distinct longitudinal phenomena rather than a single established law.

key_findings.claim: The review treats sparse-feature tracking and attribution graphs as scaling directions, while acknowledging that present explanations cover only part of model computation.
key_findings.evidence: It surveys SAE-Track, large k-sparse autoencoders, cross-layer transcoders, and attribution graphs, then states that attribution graphs yield satisfying explanations for about one quarter of analyzed prompts and that SAEs capture only fractions of computation.

key_findings.claim: The proposed safety transition—from monitoring developmental precursors to preventing unsafe circuits—is an agenda, not an empirically validated intervention result.
key_findings.evidence: Sections 6.1–6.3 use conditional examples such as detecting a future deception circuit or loss threshold; the paper reports no training intervention, predictive benchmark, false-positive analysis, or alignment experiment of its own.

method.core_idea: Narratively synthesize mechanistic-interpretability tools and longitudinal checkpoint studies under a developmental lens, then connect the resulting phenomena to cognitive analogies and proactive safety.
method.mechanism: The paper builds taxonomies and summary tables from cited literature on probes, causal tracing, circuits, SAEs, emergence, grokking, feature dynamics, and ICL transience; it does not report a systematic search protocol, inclusion criteria, or meta-analysis.
assumptions: Longitudinal changes in measured features or circuits correspond to meaningful stages of learning rather than analyzer drift or checkpoint alignment artifacts.
Mechanisms found in small/open models can inform monitoring of larger proprietary systems.
Analogies to biological development can generate useful hypotheses without implying shared mechanisms.

techniques.role: Applies a consistent interpretability measurement across training snapshots.
Uses activation or path patching to distinguish encoded information from behaviorally used computation.
Aligns sparse-autoencoder features through checkpoints to study emergence, drift, splitting, and absorption.

limitations: Author-stated: circuit analysis is difficult to automate and scale; proprietary weights block longitudinal access; universality and completeness remain unresolved.
Author-stated: SAE feature ontologies are unstable, interventions can be unnatural, and model-generated explanations can hallucinate.
Reviewer inference: the article is a narrative review with no documented database search, screening protocol, quality rubric, or reproducible evidence table.
Reviewer inference: some broad cognitive and safety conclusions are presented more confidently than the cited task- and model-specific studies warrant.
failure_modes: Feature identity can rotate or split across checkpoints, making apparent birth, death, and drift artifacts of the alignment procedure.
A predictor of capability onset in a toy task can fail under architecture, data-mixture, or post-training changes.
Targeted suppression of a correlated circuit can route computation elsewhere without removing the unsafe capability.
reusable_insights: Interpretability claims should specify whether they concern presence, causal use, algorithmic mechanism, or developmental trajectory.
Saved checkpoints turn interpretability from a post-hoc snapshot into a time series, enabling change-point and precursor tests.
A credible developmental safety program needs prospective prediction and intervention benchmarks, not only retrospective stories.
open_questions: How can features and circuits be aligned across checkpoints without assuming the ontology one hopes to discover?
Which developmental signals predict later capability robustly across seeds, scales, and data orders?
Can an intervention alter an unsafe developmental trajectory while preserving capabilities and avoiding circuit rerouting?

competitive_landscape.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety -- A Review
competitive_landscape.difference: Bereska and Gavves provide a broader causal-mechanistic safety taxonomy; this review narrows its organizing principle to how mechanisms change during training and adds cognitive-development analogies.

competitive_landscape.title: The Transient Nature of Emergent In-Context Learning in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Singh et al. experimentally demonstrate ICL-to-IWL replacement on controlled synthetic tasks; the reviewed paper generalizes that result into a broader circuit-competition narrative and safety hypothesis.

competitive_landscape.title: Tracking the Feature Dynamics in LLM Training: A Mechanistic Study
competitive_landscape.difference: SAE-Track implements longitudinal feature alignment and measures feature formation and drift; the review surveys it as one tool but contributes no new alignment method or experiment.

competitive_landscape.title: Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Sharkey et al. systematically foreground conceptual and technical open problems across mechanistic interpretability; this review emphasizes longitudinal checkpoints, capability development, and proposed proactive governance.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the article consolidates a nascent field around the formation and evolution of mechanisms and argues for developmental monitoring as a foundation for proactive safety. Reviewer inference after comparison: the developmental framing and teaching taxonomy are useful, but most technical content and open problems are inherited from existing reviews and the cited longitudinal studies; novelty is synthesis, not a systematic review, new evidence, or validated safety method.
reviewer_notes: Read all twenty-four extracted pages, including references. Findings attributed to source studies remain second-hand within this narrative review. The lack of review protocol and the distinction between demonstrated mechanisms and proposed safety uses are reviewer judgments. Competitor records were checked on primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23.
